title: Sales Analytics Report: read, clean, aggregate, top N, trend, text report

visible.label: Reads CSV file, cleans bad rows/duplicates, aggregates top N and monthly trend, formats report
visible.expectedDisplay: Dict with clean_orders=4, total_revenue=350.0, top_categories, monthly_trend, report_text
visible.script:
csv_data = """order_id,month,category,revenue,qty
O1,2026-01,Electronics,100.00,1
O1,2026-01,Electronics,999.00,5
O2,2026-02,Books,50.00,2
O3,2026-01, ,75.00,1
O4,2026-02,Home,120.00,3
O5,2026-02,Electronics,80.00,1
"""
path = "/tmp/p100_vis.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write(csv_data)
rep = build_sales_report(path, top_n=2)
assert rep["clean_orders"] == 4
assert rep["total_revenue"] == 350.0
assert rep["top_categories"] == [("Electronics", 180.0), ("Home", 120.0)]
assert rep["monthly_trend"] == [("2026-01", 100.0), ("2026-02", 250.0)]
assert "Orders: 4" in rep["report_text"]
assert "Total Revenue: $350.00" in rep["report_text"]
assert "- Electronics: $180.00" in rep["report_text"]
assert "- 2026-02: $250.00" in rep["report_text"]

visible.label: All-dirty CSV yields zero orders cleanly
visible.inputDisplay: /tmp/p100_empty.csv with negative revenue and missing fields
visible.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_empty.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write("order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\nO1,2026-01,Tech,-10,1\nO2,2026-01,,50,1\n")
rep = build_sales_report(path, top_n=3)
assert rep["clean_orders"] == 0
assert rep["total_revenue"] == 0.0
assert rep["top_categories"] == []
assert rep["monthly_trend"] == []
assert "Orders: 0" in rep["report_text"]

hidden.label: Breaks top_categories revenue ties alphabetically ascending
hidden.inputDisplay: Zed=$100, Alpha=$100, Mid=$50 with top_n=2 -> Alpha then Zed
hidden.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_tie.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write("order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\n1,2026-03,Zed,100,1\n2,2026-03,Alpha,100,1\n3,2026-03,Mid,50,1\n")
rep = build_sales_report(path, top_n=2)
assert rep["top_categories"] == [("Alpha", 100.0), ("Zed", 100.0)]

hidden.label: Drops non-positive qty or non-numeric revenue cleanly
hidden.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_bad.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write("order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\n1,2026-01,Tools,10,0\n2,2026-01,Tools,10,-2\n3,2026-01,Tools,bad,1\n4,2026-01,Tools,25.5,2\n")
rep = build_sales_report(path, top_n=1)
assert rep["clean_orders"] == 1
assert rep["total_revenue"] == 25.5

hidden.label: Chronological monthly trend sorting independent of file row order
hidden.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_months.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write("order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\n1,2026-12,A,10,1\n2,2025-11,A,20,1\n3,2026-02,A,30,1\n")
rep = build_sales_report(path)
assert rep["monthly_trend"] == [("2025-11", 20.0), ("2026-02", 30.0), ("2026-12", 10.0)]

hidden.label: Handles whitespace trimming and quoted currency revenue values
hidden.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_trim.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write('order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\n 1 , 2026-04 , Data ," $1,000.25 ", 2 \n')
rep = build_sales_report(path)
assert rep["total_revenue"] == 1000.25
assert rep["top_categories"] == [("Data", 1000.25)]

hidden.label: Exact report_text section headers and bullet structure verified
hidden.inputDisplay: Standard CSV -> report_text sections formatted cleanly
hidden.expectedDisplay: Contains Orders, Total Revenue, Top Categories, Monthly Trend headers and bullets
hidden.script:
path = "/tmp/p100_fmt.csv"
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    fp.write("order_id,month,category,revenue,qty\n1,2026-01,Cloud,125,2\n")
rep = build_sales_report(path, top_n=1)
expected_lines = [
    "Orders: 1",
    "Total Revenue: $125.00",
    "Top Categories:",
    "- Cloud: $125.00",
    "Monthly Trend:",
    "- 2026-01: $125.00",
]
assert rep["report_text"].strip().splitlines() == expected_lines

Aggregate category totals and month totals using `collections.defaultdict(float)`. Sort categories by `(-rev, category)` and slice `[:top_n]`; sort months ascending chronologically.
